chunks.text: Draw (Drawing): The act of removing a handgun from its holster. A draw is deemed to have ended when the handgun has cleared the holster.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Dry firing
chunks.title: Dry firing
chunks.text: Dry firing: The activation of the trigger and/or action of a firearm which is totally devoid of ammunition.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Dummy Ammunition
chunks.title: Dummy Ammunition
chunks.text: Dummy Ammunition: Includes practice or training rounds, blanks, snap caps and empty cases.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Engage
chunks.title: Engage
chunks.text: Engage: Firing a shot at a target. Firing a shot at, but missing, a target is not a "failure to engage". The malfunction of a firearm or a round which prevents a shot being fired, is deemed to be a "failure to engage".

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Face, (facing) uprange
chunks.title: Face, (facing) uprange
chunks.text: Face, (facing) uprange: The competitor's face, chest and toes are all facing uprange.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – False start
chunks.title: False start
chunks.text: False start: Beginning an attempt at a COF prior to the Start Signal (see Rule 8.3.4).

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Frangible target
chunks.title: Frangible target
chunks.text: Frangible target: A target, such as a clay pigeon or tile, capable of being easily broken into two or more pieces when hit.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Grain
chunks.title: Grain
chunks.text: Grain: A common unit of measurement used in respect of the weight of a bullet (1 grain = 0.0648 grams).

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Holster
chunks.title: Holster
chunks.text: Holster: A handgun retention device, worn on a competitor's belt.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Lens
chunks.title: Lens
chunks.text: Lens: A ground or molded piece of glass, plastic, or other transparent material with opposite surfaces either or both of which may be curved or flat, used in a transmissive optical device that may refract light rays.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Loaded
chunks.title: Loaded
chunks.text: Loaded: A firearm having a live or dummy round in the chamber or cylinder, or having a live or dummy round in an inserted or fitted magazine(s).

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Loading
chunks.title: Loading
chunks.text: Loading: The initial insertion of ammunition into a firearm in response to the "Load And Make Ready" command. Loading begins as soon as the competitor grips a round of ammunition, a magazine or speed loader, and ends when the firearm is securely holstered (or placed elsewhere in accordance with the written stage briefing), and the competitor's hands are clear of the firearm. For an unloaded Handgun Ready Condition, loading ends when the magazine is fully seated (or when the cylinder is fully closed).

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Location
chunks.title: Location
chunks.text: Location: A geographical place within a course of fire.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Match Personnel
chunks.title: Match Personnel
chunks.text: Match Personnel: People who have an official duty or function at a match, but who are not necessarily qualified as, or acting in the capacity of, Match Officials.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – May
chunks.title: May
chunks.text: May: Entirely optional.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Must
chunks.title: Must
chunks.text: Must: Mandatory.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – No-shoot(s)
chunks.title: No-shoot(s)
chunks.text: No-shoot(s): Target(s) that incur penalties when hit.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Not applicable
chunks.title: Not applicable
chunks.text: Not applicable: The rule or requirement does not apply to the particular discipline or Division.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – OFM
chunks.title: OFM
chunks.text: OFM: Original firearm manufacturer.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Primer
chunks.title: Primer
chunks.text: Primer: The part of a round which causes a detonation or a shot to be fired.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Props
chunks.title: Props
chunks.text: Props: Items, other than targets or Fault Lines, used in the creation, operation or decoration of a COF.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Prototype
chunks.title: Prototype
chunks.text: Prototype: A firearm in a configuration which is not in mass production and/or is not available to the general public.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Region
chunks.title: Region
chunks.text: Region: A country or other geographical area, recognized by IPSC.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Regional Director
chunks.title: Regional Director
chunks.text: Regional Director: The person, recognized by IPSC, who represents a Region.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Reloading
chunks.title: Reloading
chunks.text: Reloading: Replacement of a magazine already inserted in a firearm with a different magazine, or the insertion of additional ammunition into a firearm while the competitor is actually making his attempt at a COF. Reloading commences when the magazine (or cylinder) release button is activated, and ends when the competitor's hand is clear of the newly inserted magazine (or when the cylinder is fully closed). Exception: safely firing the chambered round at a target before inserting a fresh magazine.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Reshoot
chunks.title: Reshoot
chunks.text: Reshoot: A competitor's subsequent attempt at a course of fire, authorized in advance by a Range Officer or an Arbitration Committee.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Round
chunks.title: Round
chunks.text: Round: A cartridge of ammunition used in a handgun or rifle.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Shooting position
chunks.title: Shooting position
chunks.text: Shooting position: The physical presentation of a person's body (e.g. standing, sitting, kneeling, prone).

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Shot
chunks.title: Shot
chunks.text: Shot: A bullet which passes completely through the barrel of a firearm.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Should
chunks.title: Should
chunks.text: Should: Optional but highly recommended.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Sight picture
chunks.title: Sight picture
chunks.text: Sight picture: Aiming at a target without actually shooting at it.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Snap Cap
chunks.title: Snap Cap
chunks.text: Snap Cap: (Also "spring cap") A type of dummy round.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Squib
chunks.title: Squib
chunks.text: Squib: Any part of a round lodged inside the barrel of a firearm and/or a bullet which exits the barrel at extremely low velocity.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Stance
chunks.title: Stance
chunks.text: Stance: The physical presentation of a person's limbs (e.g. hands by the side, arms crossed etc.).

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Start position
chunks.title: Start position
chunks.text: Start position: The location, shooting position and stance prescribed by a COF prior to issuance of the Start Signal (see Rule 8.3.4).

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Strong Hand
chunks.title: Strong Hand
chunks.text: Strong Hand: The hand a person uses to initially grip a handgun when drawing it from a holster attached to their belt (the weak hand is the other hand). Competitors with only one hand can use that hand for both Strong and Weak Hand stages, subject to Rule 10.2.10.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Sweeping
chunks.title: Sweeping
chunks.text: Sweeping: Pointing the muzzle of a firearm at any part of the competitor's body during a course of fire when a handgun is held or touched while not securely holstered, or when a long gun is held while a chamber safety flag is not inserted (see Rule 10.5.5).

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Target(s)
chunks.title: Target(s)
chunks.text: Target(s): A term that can include both scoring target(s) and no-shoot(s) unless a Rule (e.g. 4.1.3) differentiates between them.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Target Array
chunks.title: Target Array
chunks.text: Target Array: A collection of approved targets that can only be seen from any single location or view.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Tie-down rig
chunks.title: Tie-down rig
chunks.text: Tie-down rig: A holster where the lower portion is secured to a competitor's leg by a strap or other means.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Unloaded
chunks.title: Unloaded
chunks.text: Unloaded: A firearm which is totally devoid of any live or dummy rounds in its chamber(s) and/or in an inserted or fitted magazine(s).

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Unloading
chunks.title: Unloading
chunks.text: Unloading: Removal of ammunition from a firearm when the competitor has completed his attempt at a COF or when otherwise directed to unload by a Range Officer. Unloading commences as soon as the magazine (or cylinder) release button is activated, and ends when the handgun is devoid of ammunition. Note that a competitor who, after activating the magazine or cylinder release button in response to the command given in Rule 8.3.6, safely fires the chambered round at a target and/or who reinserts ammunition, is deemed to have terminated the unloading process and resumed shooting.

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Uprange
chunks.title: Uprange
chunks.text: Uprange: The general area of a stage, shooting bay or range, rearwards of the default maximum safe angle of fire (see Rule 2.1.2), where the muzzle of a firearm must not be pointed during a course of fire (exception: see Rules 10.5.2 and 10.5.7).

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – View
chunks.title: View
chunks.text: View: A vantage point available at a location (e.g. one of the ports, one side of a barricade etc.).

chunks.label: Section 12.5 – Will
chunks.title: Will
chunks.text: Will: Mandatory.

chunks.label: Section 12.6
chunks.title: Measurements
chunks.text: Throughout these rules, where measurements are expressed, those in brackets are only provided as a guide.

24. International sanctioning of Level I and Level II matches is not required. However, each Regional Director is entitled to establish his own criteria and procedures for sanctioning of such matches held within his own Region.

chunks.label: Appendix A2
chunks.text:
Prior to the commencement of a match, the organizers must specify which Division(s) will be recognized.
Unless otherwise specified, IPSC sanctioned matches will recognize Divisions and Categories based on the number of registered competitors who actually compete in the match, including competitors disqualified during the match (e.g. if a Division at a Level III match has 10 competitors, but one or more are disqualified during the match, the Division will continue to be recognized), based on the following criteria:
1. Divisions:

chunks.label: Appendix A2 – Level I & II
chunks.title: Level I & II
chunks.text: Level I & II: A minimum of 5 competitors per Division (recommended).

chunks.label: Appendix A2 – Level III
chunks.title: Level III
chunks.text: Level III: A minimum of 10 competitors per Division (mandatory).

chunks.label: Appendix A2 – Level IV & V
chunks.title: Level IV & V
chunks.text:
Level IV & V: A minimum of 20 competitors per Division (mandatory).
2. Categories:
Division status must be achieved before Categories are recognized.

chunks.label: Appendix A2 – All level matches
chunks.title: All level matches
chunks.text:
All level matches: A minimum of 5 competitors per Division Category (see approved list below).
3. Individual Categories:
Categories approved for individual recognition by Division are as follows:

chunks.label: Appendix A2 – Lady
chunks.title: Lady
chunks.text: Lady: Competitors of the female gender.

chunks.label: Appendix A2 – Grand Junior
chunks.title: Grand Junior
chunks.text: Grand Junior: Competitors who are under the age of 14 until the 31st December of the year in which they become 14 years of age. A Grand Junior has the option of electing to shoot in Super Junior Category, but not in both. If there are insufficient competitors for Grand Junior Category to be recognized, all competitors registered in this Category will automatically be transferred to Super Junior Category.

chunks.label: Appendix A2 – Lady Grand Junior
chunks.title: Lady Grand Junior
chunks.text: Lady Grand Junior: Competitors of the female gender who are under the age of 14 until the 31st December of the year in which they become 14 years of age. A Lady Grand Junior has the option of electing to shoot in Lady Super Junior Category, but not in both. If there are insufficient competitors for Lady Grand Junior Category to be recognized, all competitors registered in this Category will automatically be transferred to Lady Super Junior Category.

chunks.label: Appendix A2 – Super Junior
chunks.title: Super Junior
chunks.text: Super Junior: Competitors who are under the age of 18 until the 31st December of the year in which they become 18 years of age. A Super Junior has the option of electing to shoot in Junior Category, but not in both. If there are insufficient competitors for Super Junior Category to be recognized, all competitors registered in this Category will automatically be transferred to Junior Category.

chunks.label: Appendix A2 – Lady Super Junior
chunks.title: Lady Super Junior
chunks.text: Lady Super Junior: Competitors of the female gender who are under the age of 18 until the 31st December of the year in which they become 18 years of age. A Lady Super Junior has the option of electing to shoot in Lady Junior Category, but not in both. If there are insufficient competitors for Lady Super Junior Category to be recognized, all competitors registered in this Category will automatically be transferred to Lady Junior Category.

chunks.label: Appendix A2 – Junior
chunks.title: Junior
chunks.text: Junior: Competitors who are under the age of 21 until the 31st December of the year in which they become 21 years of age.

chunks.label: Appendix A2 – Lady Junior
chunks.title: Lady Junior
chunks.text: Lady Junior: Competitors of the female gender who are under the age of 21 until the 31st December of the year in which they become 21 years of age.

chunks.label: Appendix A2 – Senior
chunks.title: Senior
chunks.text: Senior: Competitors who are over the age of 50 on the first day of the match.

chunks.label: Appendix A2 – Lady Senior
chunks.title: Lady Senior
chunks.text: Lady Senior: Competitors of the female gender who are over the age of 50 on the first day of the match. A Lady Senior has the option of electing to shoot in Lady Category, but not in both. If there are insufficient competitors for Lady Senior Category to be recognized, all competitors registered in this Category will automatically be transferred to Lady Category.

chunks.label: Appendix A2 – Super Senior
chunks.title: Super Senior
chunks.text: Super Senior: Competitors who are over the age of 60 on the first day of the match. A Super Senior has the option of electing to shoot in Senior Category, but not in both. If there are insufficient competitors for Super Senior Category to be recognized, all competitors registered in this Category will automatically be transferred to Senior Category.

chunks.label: Appendix A2 – Grand Senior
chunks.title: Grand Senior
chunks.text:
Grand Senior: Competitors who are over the age of 70 on the first day of the match. A Grand Senior has the option of electing to shoot in Super Senior Category, but not in both. If there are insufficient competitors for Grand Senior Category to be recognized, all competitors registered in this Category will automatically be transferred to Super Senior Category.
4. Team Categories:
IPSC Level IV & V matches must recognize any of the following Team Categories for team awards when a minimum of 3 teams are registered in the Category.
IPSC Level I, II & III matches may recognize the following for team awards: (a) Regional teams by Division. (b) Regional teams by Division for Lady Category. (c) Regional teams by Division for Grand Junior Category. (d) Regional teams by Division for Lady Grand Junior Category. (e) Regional teams by Division for Super Junior Category. (f) Regional teams by Division for Lady Super Junior Category. (g) Regional teams by Division for Junior Category. (h) Regional teams by Division for Lady Junior Category (i) Regional teams by Division for Senior Category. (j) Regional teams by Division for Lady Senior Category. (k) Regional teams by Division for Super Senior Category. (l) Regional teams by Division for Grand Senior Category. (m) Teams by Family. Family Teams consist of two members, one being either a Grand Junior, Lady Grand Junior, Super Junior, Lady Super Junior, Junior or Lady Junior and the other either a parent or grandparent of the Grand Junior, Lady Grand Junior, Super Junior, Lady Super Junior, Junior or Lady Junior. Notwithstanding Rules 6.4.2 and 6.4.2.1, one of the team members may also be a member of a Regional Team and the two team members may compete in different Divisions and a female individually registered as "Lady" may participate as the Lady Grand Junior, Lady Super Junior or Lady Junior provided that she satisfies the appropriate age limit. Family Team results will be calculated by adding the match percentiles attained by the two members. There may be more than one Family Team entered per Region.

chunks.label: Appendix C1, item 1
chunks.chapter: Appendix C1: Calibration of IPSC Poppers
chunks.text: The Range Master must designate a specific supply of ammunition and one or more firearms to be used as official calibration tools by officials authorized by him to serve as calibration officers.

chunks.label: Appendix C1, item 2
chunks.chapter: Appendix C1: Calibration of IPSC Poppers
chunks.text: Prior to commencement of a match, the power factor of the calibration ammunition must be measured using the procedure specified in Rule 5.6.3.3, except that only 4 rounds for each calibration firearm are required. The calibration ammunition, when tested through each designated firearm, must achieve a power factor of between 120 to 125 to qualify.

chunks.label: Appendix C1, item 3
chunks.chapter: Appendix C1: Calibration of IPSC Poppers
chunks.text: Once the supply of ammunition and the designated firearms have been tested and approved by the Range Master, they are not subject to challenge by competitors.

chunks.label: Appendix C1, item 4
chunks.chapter: Appendix C1: Calibration of IPSC Poppers
chunks.text: The Range Master must arrange for each popper to be calibrated prior to commencement of a match, and whenever required during a match.

chunks.label: Appendix C1, item 5
chunks.chapter: Appendix C1: Calibration of IPSC Poppers
chunks.text: For initial calibration, each popper must be set to fall when hit within the calibration zone with a single shot fired from a designated firearm using the calibration ammunition. The shot must be fired from the shooting location in the course of fire furthest from where at least part of the calibration zone of the popper being calibrated is visible to competitors. Calibration zones are indicated in the diagrams in the following pages.

chunks.label: Appendix C1, item 6
chunks.chapter: Appendix C1: Calibration of IPSC Poppers
chunks.text:
If, during a course of fire, a popper does not fall when hit, a competitor has three alternatives:
(a) The popper is shot again until it falls. In this case, no further action is required and the course of fire is scored "as shot".
(b) The popper is left standing but the competitor does not challenge the calibration. In this case, no further action is required and the course of fire is scored "as shot", with the subject popper scored as a miss.
(c) The popper is left standing and the competitor challenges the calibration. In this case, the popper and the surrounding area on which it stands must not be touched or interfered with by any person. If a Match Official violates this rule, the competitor must reshoot the course of fire. If the competitor or any other person violates this rule, the popper will be scored as a miss and the rest of the course of fire will be scored "as shot".
(d) If the popper falls for any other reason (e.g. wind action), before it can be calibrated, a reshoot must be ordered.

chunks.label: Appendix C1, item 7
chunks.chapter: Appendix C1: Calibration of IPSC Poppers
chunks.text:
In the absence of any interference, a calibration officer must conduct a calibration test of the subject popper (when required under 6(c) above), from as near as possible to the point from where the competitor shot the popper, when the following will apply:
(a) If the first shot fired by the calibration officer hits the calibration zone or below and the popper falls, the popper is deemed to be properly calibrated, and it will be scored as a miss.
(b) If the first shot fired by the calibration officer hits the calibration zone or below and the popper does not fall, the popper is deemed to have failed and the competitor must be ordered to reshoot the course of fire, once the popper has been recalibrated.
(c) If the first shot fired by the calibration officer misses the popper altogether, another shot must be fired until one of 7(a) or 7(b) occurs.

chunks.label: Appendix C1, item 8
chunks.chapter: Appendix C1: Calibration of IPSC Poppers
chunks.text: Note that authorized metal plates are not subject to calibration or challenge (see Rule 4.3.3.2).

chunks.label: Appendix D3, item 17
chunks.text: Handguns must be based on and visibly resemble the profile and contours of the classic 1911-genre design. This means a single-stack, one piece metal frame, slide with stirrup cuts, and a dust cover (with or without an accessory rail) which has a maximum length of 75 mm when measured from the leading edge of the dust cover to the rear of the slide stop pin.

chunks.label: Appendix D3, item 17.1
chunks.text: Magazine wells cannot exceed a maximum outside width of 35 mm. Compliance is checked by way of a 35 mm wide, and at least 5 mm deep, notch carved into the outside of the box, or by use of a ruler or caliper, as approved by the officiating Range Master.

chunks.label: Appendix D3, item 18
chunks.text: Prohibited modifications / parts are slide lightening cuts, weak hand thumb rests and slide rackers.

chunks.label: Appendix D3, item 19
chunks.text: Permitted modifications are shaped slides (flat-top, tri-top etc.), shaped trigger guards (squared, undercut etc.), bob-tail backstraps, bull or coned barrels, external extractors, finger-grooves (machined, add-on, wrap-around etc.), custom magazine release buttons, triggers, hammers, single/ambidextrous thumb safeties, any open sights (which may be embedded into the slide), and extended slide lock levers and thumb shields provided they do not act as a thumb rest.

chunks.label: Appendix D3, item 19.1
chunks.text: Other modifications permitted include those of a cosmetic nature (e.g. custom grip panels, scrimshaw or similar surface engravings, checkering, serrations etc.).

chunks.label: Appendix D3, item 20

chunks.label: Appendix D4, item 16
chunks.text: The minimum trigger pull must either be 2.27kg (5lbs.) for the first shot fired and no restriction for subsequent shots fired, or 1.36kg (3lbs.) for every shot fired.

chunks.label: Appendix D4, item 17
chunks.text: Handguns with external hammers must be fully decocked (see Rule 8.1.2.5), at the Start Signal. First shot attempted must be double action. Competitors in this Division who, after the issuance of the Start Signal and prior to attempting the first shot, cock the hammer on a handgun which has a loaded chamber, will incur one procedural penalty per occurrence. Note that a procedural penalty will not be assessed in respect of courses of fire where the ready condition requires the competitor to prepare the handgun with an empty chamber. In these cases, the competitor may fire the first shot single action.

chunks.label: Appendix D4, item 18
chunks.text: Original parts and components offered by the OFM as standard equipment, or as an option, for a specific model handgun on the IPSC approved handgun list are permitted, subject to the following:

chunks.label: Appendix D4, item 18.1
chunks.text: Modifications to them, other than minor detailing (the removal of burrs and/or adjustments unavoidably required in order to fit replacement OFM parts or components), are prohibited. Other prohibited modifications include:  Those which facilitate faster reloading (e.g. grip panels, racking or cocking handles, flared, enlarged and/or add-on magwells, etc.);  Weak hand thumb rests. Changing the original color and/or finish of a handgun, and/or adding stripes, stippling, thumb shields (provided they do not act as a thumb rest) or other embellishments is permitted. Extended slide lock levers are prohibited.

chunks.label: Appendix D4, item 18.2
chunks.text: Magazines accessible to a competitor during a COF must not contain more than 15 rounds at the Start Signal. Identifying marks or decals, internal capacity limiters, bumper pads and additional witness holes, which add or remove negligible weight to/from magazines, are permitted.

chunks.label: Appendix D4, item 18.3
chunks.text: Sights may be trimmed, adjusted and/or have colors applied. Sights may also be fitted with fiber optic or similar inserts.

chunks.label: Appendix D4, item 19
chunks.text: Aftermarket parts, components and accessories are prohibited, except as follows:

chunks.label: Appendix D4, item 19.1
chunks.text: Aftermarket magazines are permitted, subject to 18.2 above.

chunks.label: Appendix D4, item 19.2
chunks.text: Aftermarket open sights (see Rule 5.1.3.1) are permitted, provided their installation and/or adjustment requires no alteration to the handgun.

chunks.label: Appendix D4, item 19.3
chunks.text: Aftermarket grip panels which do not protrude beyond the bottom of the frame and/or the application of tape on grips (see Appendix E3a) are permitted. However, rubber sleeves are prohibited.

chunks.label: Appendix D4, item 19.4
chunks.text: Aftermarket springs are permitted, provided they are in the same configuration as original.

chunks.label: Appendix D4, item 19.5
chunks.text: Aftermarket trigger assemblies are permitted, subject to 16 above. A trigger assembly is defined as a mechanism that, once the trigger is pulled, activates the firing sequence of a firearm. Note that, if the original trigger includes a trigger safety, then the aftermarket trigger must also include a trigger safety.

chunks.label: Appendix D4, item 19.6
chunks.text: Aftermarket hammers are permitted.

chunks.label: Appendix E4a
chunks.chapter: Appendix E4a: Trigger Pull Testing Procedure
chunks.text: When a minimum trigger pull is required by a Division, handguns will be tested as follows:

chunks.label: Appendix E4a, item 1
chunks.chapter: Appendix E4a: Trigger Pull Testing Procedure
chunks.text: The unloaded handgun will be prepared as if the handgun is ready to fire a double action shot;

chunks.label: Appendix E4a, item 2
chunks.chapter: Appendix E4a: Trigger Pull Testing Procedure
chunks.text: The trigger weight or scale will be attached as closely as possible to the center of the trigger face;

chunks.label: Appendix E4a, item 3
chunks.chapter: Appendix E4a: Trigger Pull Testing Procedure

chunks.label: Appendix E4a, item 4
chunks.chapter: Appendix E4a: Trigger Pull Testing Procedure
chunks.text: One of the above tests will be conducted a maximum of 3 times;

chunks.label: Appendix E4a, item 5
chunks.chapter: Appendix E4a: Trigger Pull Testing Procedure
chunks.text: If the hammer or striker does not fall on any 1 of the 3 attempts in 3(a) above, or if the scale registers not less than 2.27kg (5lbs.) in 3(b) above, the handgun has passed the test;

chunks.label: Appendix E4a, item 6
chunks.chapter: Appendix E4a: Trigger Pull Testing Procedure
chunks.text: If the hammer or striker falls on all three (3) attempts in 3(a) above, or if the scale registers less than 2.27kg (5lbs.) in 3(b) above, the handgun has failed the test and, unless it passes the 1.36kg (3lbs.) for Every Shot test below, Rule 6.2.5.1 will apply.

chunks.chapter: Appendix E4a: Trigger Pull Testing Procedure

chunks.chapter: Appendix E4a: Trigger Pull Testing Procedure
chunks.text: The trigger weight or scale will be attached as closely as possible to the center of the trigger face;

chunks.text: One of the above tests will be conducted a maximum of 3 times;

chunks.label: Appendix E4a, item 5
chunks.chapter: Appendix E4a: Trigger Pull Testing Procedure
chunks.text: If the hammer or striker does not fall on any 1 of the 3 attempts in 3(a) above, or if the scale registers not less than 1.36kg (3lbs.) in 3(b) above, the handgun has passed the test;

chunks.label: Appendix E4a, item 6
chunks.chapter: Appendix E4a: Trigger Pull Testing Procedure
chunks.text: If the hammer or striker falls on all three (3) attempts in 3(a) above, or if the scale registers less than 1.36kg (3lbs.) in 3(b) above, the handgun has failed the test and, unless it passes the 2.27kg (5lbs.) for the First Shot test above, Rule 6.2.5.1 will apply.

chunks.label: Appendix E4b
chunks.chapter: Appendix E4b: Barrel Length Measurement Protocol
chunks.text:
A fully assembled and unloaded handgun is pointed vertically skywards, then a dowel with a 127 mm marker is inserted into the muzzle end of the barrel until the dowel rests on the breech face. If the 127 mm marker is at or beyond the muzzle end of the barrel, the handgun is compliant for Production Division.
For revolvers, measure from the muzzle end of the barrel to the face of the forcing cone where the barrel ends. If the length is 127 mm or less, the revolver is compliant for Production Division.

chunks.label: Rule 1.1.1
chunks.title: Safety
chunks.text: Safety – IPSC matches must be designed, constructed and conducted with due consideration to safety.

chunks.label: Rule 1.1.2
chunks.title: Quality
chunks.text: Quality – The value of an IPSC match is determined by the quality of the challenge presented in the course design. Courses of fire must be designed primarily to test a competitor's IPSC shooting skills, not their physical abilities.

chunks.label: Rule 1.1.3
chunks.title: Balance
chunks.text: Balance – Accuracy, Power and Speed are equivalent elements of IPSC shooting, and are expressed in the Latin words "Diligentia, Vis, Celeritas" ("DVC"). A properly balanced course of fire will depend largely upon the nature of the challenges presented therein. However, courses must be designed, and IPSC matches must be conducted in such a way, as to evaluate these elements equally.

chunks.label: Rule 1.1.4
chunks.title: Diversity
chunks.text: Diversity – IPSC shooting challenges are diverse. While it is not necessary to construct new courses for each match, no single course of fire must be repeated to allow its use to be considered a definitive measure of IPSC shooting skills.

chunks.label: Rule 1.1.5
chunks.title: Freestyle
chunks.text: Freestyle – IPSC matches are freestyle. Competitors must be permitted to solve the challenge presented in a freestyle manner and, for handgun and shotgun matches, to shoot targets on an "as and when visible" basis. After the Start Signal, courses of fire must not require mandatory reloads nor dictate a shooting position, location or stance, except as specified below. However, conditions may be created, and barriers or other physical limitations may be constructed, to compel a competitor into shooting positions, locations or stances.

chunks.label: Rule 1.1.5.1
chunks.text: Level I and Level II matches are not required to comply strictly with the freestyle requirements or round count limitations (see Section 1.2).

chunks.label: Rule 1.1.5.2
chunks.text: Short Courses and Classifiers may include mandatory reloads and may dictate a shooting position, location and/or stance. When a mandatory reload is required, it must be completed after the competitor shoots at his first target, and before he shoots at his final target. Violations are subject to one procedural penalty.

chunks.label: Rule 1.1.5.3
chunks.text: Short Courses and Classifiers may specify that only the weak shoulder is to be used when shooting.

chunks.label: Rule 1.1.5.4
chunks.text: If a written stage briefing specifies that a competitor is required to carry, retain or grasp an object during his attempt at a course of fire, Rule 10.2.2 will apply.

chunks.label: Rule 1.1.5.5
chunks.text: Course Designers may give competitors freedom to await the Start Signal anywhere within the boundaries of a well demarcated firing zone.

chunks.label: Rule 1.1.6
chunks.title: Difficulty
chunks.text: Difficulty – IPSC matches present varied degrees of difficulty. No shooting challenge may be appealed as being prohibitive. This does not apply to non-shooting challenges, which should reasonably allow for differences in competitor's height and physical build.

chunks.label: Rule 1.1.7
chunks.title: Challenge
chunks.text: Challenge – IPSC matches recognize the challenges presented when using full power firearms in dynamic shooting, and must always employ a minimum power factor to be attained by all competitors to reflect this challenge.

chunks.label: Section 1.2
chunks.title: Types of Courses
chunks.text: IPSC matches may contain the following types of courses of fire:

chunks.label: Rule 1.2.1
chunks.title: General Courses of Fire
chunks.text: General Courses of Fire:

chunks.label: Rule 1.2.1.1
chunks.title: Short Courses
chunks.text: Short Courses – Must not require more than 8 rounds to complete and are restricted to a maximum of 12 scoring hits.

chunks.label: Rule 1.2.1.2
chunks.title: Medium Courses
chunks.text: Medium Courses – Must not require more than 16 rounds to complete and are restricted to a maximum of 24 scoring hits. Course design and construction must not require more than 8 rounds to be shot from any single location or view.

chunks.label: Rule 1.2.1.3
chunks.title: Long Courses
chunks.text: Long Courses – Must not require more than 28 rounds to complete and are restricted to a maximum of 32 scoring hits. Course design and construction must not require more than 8 rounds to be shot from any single location or view. A COF requiring 24 or more rounds must not stipulate an unloaded gun as a start condition.

chunks.label: Rule 1.2.1.4
chunks.text: The approved balance for an IPSC sanctioned match is a ratio of 3 Short Courses to 2 Medium Courses to 1 Long Course (see Approved Stage Ratios in Appendix A4).

chunks.label: Rule 1.2.1.5
chunks.text: Empty chamber and/or empty magazine well/cylinder firearm ready conditions (see Chapter 8), should not be required for more than 25% of the courses of fire in a match.

chunks.label: Rule 1.2.2
chunks.title: Special Courses of Fire
chunks.text: Special Courses of Fire:

chunks.label: Rule 1.2.2.1
chunks.title: Classifiers
chunks.text: Classifiers – Courses of fire authorized by a Regional Director and/or IPSC, which are available to competitors seeking a regional and/or international classification. Classifiers must be set up in accordance with these rules and be conducted strictly in accordance with the notes and diagrams accompanying them. Results must be submitted to the authorizing entity in the format required (with the applicable fees, if any), in order for them to be recognized.

chunks.label: Rule 1.2.2.2
chunks.title: Shoot-Off
chunks.text: Shoot-Off – An event conducted separately from a match. Two eligible competitors simultaneously engage two identical and adjacent target arrays in a process of one or more elimination bouts (see Appendix A3). It is recommended that metal targets be used, and that the final target for each competitor is set so that it overlaps that of the other competitor when struck down, with the winner being the competitor whose target is on the bottom. Each target array must not exceed 8 rounds and each competitor may be required to perform a mandatory reload after shooting at his first target, and before he shoots at his final target. Violations are subject to automatic forfeiture of the bout.

chunks.label: Rule 1.3.1
chunks.text: Match organizers wishing to receive IPSC sanctioning must comply with the general principles of course design and course construction as well as all other current IPSC Rules and regulations relevant to the discipline. Courses of fire that do not comply with these requirements will not be sanctioned, and must not be publicized or announced as IPSC sanctioned matches.

chunks.label: Rule 1.3.2
chunks.text: Target arrays and presentations or props included in courses of fire submitted to IPSC, but deemed by IPSC to be illogical or impractical, will not be approved (see latest version of the separate Target Array Book).

chunks.label: Rule 1.3.3
chunks.text: The IPSC President, his delegate, or an officer of the Confederation (in that order), may withdraw IPSC sanctioning from a match if, in his or their opinion, a match or any component part thereof:

chunks.label: Rule 1.3.3.1
chunks.text: Contravenes the purpose or spirit of the principles of course design; or

chunks.label: Rule 1.3.3.2
chunks.text: Has been constructed at significant variance to the sanctioned design; or

chunks.label: Rule 1.3.3.3
chunks.title: Is in breach of any current IPSC Rules; or
chunks.text: Is in breach of any current IPSC Rules; or

chunks.label: Rule 1.3.3.4
chunks.text: Is likely to bring the sport of IPSC shooting into disrepute; or

chunks.label: Rule 1.3.3.5
chunks.text: If the provisions of Rule 6.5.1.1 have not been observed.

chunks.label: Rule 1.3.4
chunks.text: IPSC match level requirements and recommendations are specified in Appendix A1.

chunks.label: Rule 2.1.1
chunks.title: Physical Construction
chunks.text: Physical Construction – Safety considerations in the design, physical construction, and stated requirements for any course of fire are the responsibility of the host organization subject to the approval of the Range Master. Reasonable effort must be made to prevent injury to competitors, officials and spectators during the match. Course design should prevent inadvertent unsafe actions wherever possible. Consideration must be given to the operation of any course of fire to provide suitable access for officials supervising the competitors.

chunks.label: Rule 2.1.2
chunks.title: Safe Angles of Fire
chunks.text: Safe Angles of Fire – Courses of fire must always be constructed taking into account safe angles of fire. Consideration must be given to safe target and frame construction and the angle of any possible ricochets. Where appropriate the physical dimensions and suitability of backstops and side berms must be determined as part of the construction process. Unless otherwise specified, the default maximum muzzle angle is 90 degrees in all directions, measured from the front of the competitor facing directly center downrange. Violations are subject to Rule 10.5.2.

chunks.label: Rule 2.1.2.1
chunks.text: Subject to the direction and approval of the Regional Director, stage(s) or range specific muzzle angles (reduced or increased) may be permitted. Violations are subject to Rule 10.5.2. Full details of the applicable angles and any conditional factors (e.g. a reduced vertical muzzle angle only applies when a finger is inside the trigger guard), should be published in advance of the match and must be included in the written stage briefings (also see Section 2.3).

chunks.label: Rule 2.1.3
chunks.title: Minimum Distances
chunks.text: Minimum Distances – Whenever metal targets or metal hard cover are used in a course of fire, minimum distances apply while they are being shot. Where possible, this should be done with physical barriers. If Fault Lines are used to limit the approach to metal targets, they must be placed further away so that the competitor may inadvertently fault the line and still be outside the minimum distance (see Rule 10.4.7). Care should also be taken in respect of metal props in the line of fire.

chunks.label: Rule 2.1.3.1
chunks.title: Minimum Distances for Shooting Birdshot and Buckshot
chunks.text: Minimum Distances for Shooting Birdshot and Buckshot – The minimum distance is 5 meters. Fault Lines must be placed at least 6 meters from the targets or metal hard cover.

chunks.label: Rule 2.1.3.2
chunks.title: Minimum Distances for Shooting Slugs
chunks.text: Minimum Distances for Shooting Slugs – The minimum distance is 40 meters. Fault Lines must be placed at least 41 meters from the targets or metal hard cover.

chunks.label: Rule 2.1.4
chunks.title: Target Locations
chunks.text: Target Locations – When a course is constructed to include target locations other than immediately downrange, organizers and officials must protect or restrict surrounding areas to which competitors, officials or spectators have access. Each competitor must be permitted to solve the competitive problem in his own way and must not be hindered by being forced to act in any manner which might cause unsafe action. Targets must be arranged so that shooting at them as presented will not cause competitors to breach safe angles of fire.

chunks.label: Rule 2.1.5
chunks.title: Range Surface
chunks.text: Range Surface – Where possible, the range surface must be prepared prior to the match, and be kept moderately clear of debris during the match, to provide reasonable safety for competitors and officials. Consideration should be given to the possibility of inclement weather and competitor actions. Match Officials may add gravel, sand or other materials to a deteriorated range surface at any time, and such range maintenance actions may not be appealed by competitors.

chunks.label: Rule 2.1.6
chunks.title: Obstacles
chunks.text: Obstacles – Natural or created obstacles in a course of fire should reasonably allow for variations in competitors' height and physical build and should be constructed to provide reasonable safety for all competitors, Match Officials and spectators.

chunks.label: Rule 2.1.7
chunks.title: Common Firing Lines
chunks.text: Common Firing Lines – Courses of fire where multiple competitors are required to fire simultaneously from a common firing line (e.g. Shoot-Off), must provide a minimum of 3 meters of free space between each competitor.

chunks.label: Rule 2.1.8
chunks.title: Target Placement
chunks.text: Target Placement – Care must be taken with the physical placement of a paper target to prevent a "shoot through".

chunks.label: Rule 2.1.8.1
chunks.text: Target placement should be clearly marked on the target stands for target replacement and target stands should be securely fixed or their locations should be clearly marked on the range surface to ensure consistency throughout the entire match. Furthermore, target types should be specified and identified on the target frames or stands prior to the start of the match to ensure that a scoring target is not interchanged with a no-shoot after the match has commenced.

chunks.label: Rule 2.1.8.2
chunks.text: When paper and metal targets are used in close proximity in a course of fire, care must be taken to minimize the risk of splatter from metal targets.

chunks.label: Rule 2.1.8.3
chunks.text: When IPSC Poppers are used in a course of fire, care should be taken to ensure that the location or foundation area is prepared to provide consistent operation throughout the match.

chunks.label: Rule 2.1.8.4
chunks.text: Static targets (i.e. those which are not activated) must not be presented at an angle greater than 90 degrees from the vertical.

chunks.label: Rule 2.1.9
chunks.title: Berms
chunks.text: Berms – All berms are "off limits" to all persons at all times, except when access to them is specifically permitted by a Range Officer (see Section 10.6).

chunks.label: Rule 2.1.10
chunks.title: Detachable Wads
chunks.text: Detachable Wads – Some types of slug ammunition have detachable wads and in buckshot cartridges the wads separate from the pellets. In view of this paper targets should either be "backed" (e.g. with plywood or another product of a suitable thickness), or placed at a greater distance. 10 meters is recommended in the case of buckshot, to prevent such wads penetrating paper targets.

chunks.label: Rule 2.1.11
chunks.title: Birdshot Ammunition with Paper Targets
chunks.text: Birdshot Ammunition with Paper Targets – A competitor must never be required to engage paper targets using birdshot ammunition.

chunks.label: Rule 2.1.12
chunks.title: Permitted Ammunition
chunks.text: Permitted Ammunition – Courses of fire must nominate a single permitted type of ammunition, i.e. birdshot, buckshot or slugs.

chunks.label: Section 2.2
chunks.title: Course Construction Criteria
chunks.text: During the construction of a course of fire, a variety of physical barriers may be used to restrict competitor movement and to provide additional competitive challenges as follows:

chunks.label: Rule 2.2.1
chunks.title: Fault Lines
chunks.text: Fault Lines – Competitor movement should preferably be restricted through the use of physical barriers. However, the use of Fault Lines is permitted as follows:

chunks.label: Rule 2.2.1.1
chunks.text: To prevent unsafe and/or unrealistic charging at, or retreat from, targets;

chunks.label: Rule 2.2.1.2
chunks.text: To simulate the use of physical barriers and/or cover;

chunks.label: Rule 2.2.1.3
chunks.text: To define the boundaries of a general shooting area or part thereof.

chunks.label: Rule 2.2.1.4
chunks.text: Fault Lines must be fixed firmly in place, they must rise at least 2 centimeters above ground level, they should be constructed of wood or other rigid materials, and they should be of a consistent color (preferably red), at every COF in a match. Unless used in a continuous manner to define the boundary of a general shooting area, Fault Lines must be a minimum of 1.5 meters in length, but they are deemed to extend to infinity.

chunks.label: Rule 2.2.1.5
chunks.text: If a COF has a passageway visibly delineated by Fault Lines and/or a clearly demarcated shooting area, any competitor who takes a shortcut by stepping on the ground outside the passageway and/or shooting area will incur one procedural penalty for each shot fired after beginning the shortcut.

chunks.label: Rule 2.2.2
chunks.text: Not applicable.

chunks.label: Rule 2.2.3
chunks.title: Barriers
chunks.text: Barriers – Must be constructed in the following manner:

chunks.label: Rule 2.2.3.1
chunks.text: They must be high enough and strong enough to serve the intended purpose. Unless supplemented by a shooting platform or similar, barriers of at least 1.8 meters high are deemed to extend skywards to infinity (also see Rule 10.2.11).

chunks.label: Rule 2.2.3.2
chunks.text: They should include Fault Lines projecting rearward at ground level from the side edges.

chunks.label: Rule 2.2.4
chunks.text: Not applicable.

chunks.label: Rule 2.2.5
chunks.title: Cooper Tunnels
chunks.text: Cooper Tunnels – Are tunnels comprised of braced uprights supporting loose overhead materials (e.g. wooden slats), which may fall off when inadvertently dislodged by competitors (see Rule 10.2.5). These tunnels may be constructed to any height, but overhead materials must not be heavy enough to cause injury if they fall.

chunks.label: Rule 2.2.6
chunks.title: Stage Props
chunks.text: Stage Props – Where these items are intended to support a competitor in motion or while shooting targets, they must be constructed with the safety of the competitor and Match Officials as a priority. Provisions must be made to allow Match Officials to safely monitor and control competitor action at all times. Props must be strong enough to withstand use by all competitors.

chunks.label: Rule 2.2.7
chunks.title: Windows and Ports
chunks.text: Windows and Ports – Must be placed at a height reachable by most competitors, with a sturdy platform being available for use by others, if requested, without penalty.

chunks.label: Rule 2.3.1
chunks.text: Match Officials may, for any reason, modify the physical construction or stage procedure for a course of fire, provided that such changes are approved in advance by the Range Master. Any such physical changes or additions to a published course of fire should be completed before the stage begins.

chunks.label: Rule 2.3.2
chunks.text: All competitors must be notified of any such changes as soon as possible. As a minimum, they must be notified by the official in charge of the course of fire during the squad briefing.

chunks.label: Rule 2.3.3
chunks.text: If the Range Master approves any such action after the match begins he must either:

chunks.label: Rule 2.3.3.1
chunks.text: Allow the course of fire to continue with the modification affecting only those competitors who have not already completed the stage. If a competitor's actions caused the change, that competitor must be required to reshoot the revised course of fire, subject to Rule 2.3.4.1; or

chunks.label: Rule 2.3.3.2
chunks.text: If possible, require all competitors to complete the course of fire as revised with all previous attempts removed from the match results.

chunks.label: Rule 2.3.3.3
chunks.text: A competitor who refuses to reshoot a course of fire, under this or any other Section, when so ordered by a Range Officer, will receive a zero score for that stage, irrespective of any previous attempt.

chunks.label: Rule 2.3.4
chunks.text: If the Range Master (in consultation with the Match Director) determines that the physical or procedural change results in a loss of competitive equity and it is impossible for all competitors to attempt the revised stage, or if the stage has been rendered unsuitable or unworkable for any reason, that stage and all associated competitor scores must be deleted from the match.

chunks.label: Rule 2.3.4.1
chunks.text: A competitor who incurred a disqualification in a stage which is subsequently deleted, may be entitled to reinstatement, if the highest level of appeal pursued by the competitor (i.e. the Range Master or the Arbitration Committee, as the case may be), deems that the disqualification was directly attributable to the reasons for the stage being deleted.

chunks.label: Rule 2.3.5
chunks.text: During inclement weather, the Range Master may order that paper targets be fitted with transparent protective covers and/or overhead shelters, and this order is not subject to appeal by competitors (see Rule 6.6.1). Such items must be applied and remain fitted to all affected targets for the same period of time, until the order is rescinded by the Range Master.

chunks.label: Rule 2.3.6
chunks.text: If the Range Master (in consultation with the Match Director) deems that climatic or other conditions have, or are likely to, seriously affect the safety and/or conduct of a match, he may order that all shooting activities be suspended, until he issues a "resume shooting" directive.

chunks.label: Rule 2.4.1
chunks.text: The host organization is responsible for the construction and placement of a sufficient number of Safety Areas for the match. They should be conveniently placed and must be easily identified with signs.

chunks.label: Rule 2.4.2
chunks.text: Safety Areas must include a table with the safe muzzle direction and boundaries clearly shown. If a backstop and/or side walls are included, they must be constructed of materials capable of containing fired rounds. Safety Areas at tournaments and long gun matches must include sufficient gun racks adjacent to, but not in, the Safety Area for secure muzzle-up storage of rifles and shotguns.

chunks.label: Rule 2.4.3
chunks.text: Competitors are permitted to use Safety Areas unsupervised for the activities stated below provided they remain within the boundaries of the Safety Area and the firearm is pointed in a safe direction. Violations may be subject to disqualification (see Rule 10.5.1).

chunks.label: Rule 2.4.3.1
chunks.text: Casing, uncasing, and holstering unloaded firearms.

chunks.label: Rule 2.4.3.2
chunks.text: Practice the mounting, drawing, dry firing and re-holstering of unloaded firearms.

chunks.label: Rule 2.4.3.3
chunks.text: Practice the insertion and removal of empty magazines and/or to cycle the action of a firearm.

chunks.label: Rule 2.4.3.4
chunks.text: Conduct inspections, stripping, cleaning, repairs and maintenance of firearms, component parts and other accessories.

chunks.label: Rule 2.4.4
chunks.text: Dummy ammunition and live rounds, whether loose, packaged or contained in magazines or speed loaders, must not be handled in a Safety Area under any circumstances (see Rule 10.5.13).

chunks.label: Rule 2.5.1
chunks.text: When available at a match, a test firing bay must be operated under the supervision and control of a Range Officer.

chunks.label: Rule 2.5.2
chunks.text: Competitors may test the operation of their firearm and ammunition, subject to all existing safety rules and any time limits or other restrictions imposed by a Range Officer.

chunks.label: Rule 2.5.3
chunks.text: At Level III or higher tournaments and long gun matches, approved IPSC paper and metal targets (where possible, electronically indicating or self-resetting), should be available for use by competitors to aid in the sighting-in of their firearms, in accordance with the guidelines shown in Appendix C3.

chunks.label: Rule 2.6.1
chunks.text: Vendors (i.e. individuals, corporations and other entities displaying or selling merchandise at an IPSC match) are solely responsible for the safe handling and security of their products and other items in their care, and ensuring they are displayed in a condition that will not endanger any person. Assembled firearms must be deactivated prior to being displayed.

chunks.label: Rule 2.6.2
chunks.text: The Range Master (in consultation with the Match Director) must clearly delineate the vendor area, and he may issue "Acceptable Practice Guidelines" to all vendors, who are responsible for their implementation in respect of their own merchandise.

chunks.label: Rule 2.6.3
chunks.text: Competitors may handle unloaded vendor's firearms while remaining wholly within the vendor areas, provided reasonable care is taken to ensure that the muzzle is not pointed at any person while being handled.

chunks.label: Rule 2.7.1
chunks.text: A sufficient number of hygiene areas, with hand cleansing supplies and facilities, should be provided adjacent to lavatories and near the entrance to food service areas.

chunks.label: Section 3.1
chunks.title: General Regulations
chunks.text: The competitor is always responsible to safely fulfill the requirements of a course of fire but can only reasonably be expected to do so after verbally or physically receiving the written stage briefing, which must adequately explain the requirements to the competitors. Course information can be broadly divided into the following types:

chunks.label: Rule 3.1.1
chunks.title: Published Courses of Fire
chunks.text: Published Courses of Fire – Registered competitors and/or their Regional Directors must be provided with the same course of fire information, within the same notice period, in advance of the match. The information may be provided by physical or electronic means, or by reference to a website (also see Section 2.3).

chunks.label: Rule 3.1.2
chunks.title: Non-Published Courses of Fire
chunks.text: Non-Published Courses of Fire – Same as Rule 3.1.1 except that the details for the course of fire are not published beforehand. The course of fire instructions are provided in the written stage briefing.

chunks.label: Rule 3.2.1
chunks.text:
A written stage briefing consistent with these rules and approved by the Range Master must be posted at each course of fire prior to commencement of the match. This briefing will take precedence over any course of fire information published or otherwise communicated to competitors in advance of the match, and it must provide the following minimum information:
 Scoring targets (type & number);  Target distances and balance (Rifle, Mini Rifle and Pistol Caliber Carbine matches only);  Minimum number of rounds required;  Ammunition type (Shotgun matches only);  Number of scoring hits for paper targets (if not the default);  Firearm ready condition (see Section 8.1);  Competitor ready condition (see Rule 3.2.2, Section 8.2 and Appendix E1/E2);  Start position;  Time starts: audible or visual signal;  Procedure.

chunks.label: Rule 3.2.2
chunks.text: The Range Officer in charge of a course of fire must read out the written stage briefing verbatim to each squad. The Range Officer must visually demonstrate the acceptable Start Position (either by use of a picture or physically) at all match levels.

chunks.label: Rule 3.2.3
chunks.text: The Range Master may modify a written stage briefing at any time for reasons of clarity, consistency or safety (see Section 2.3).

chunks.label: Rule 3.2.4
chunks.text: After the written stage briefing has been read to competitors, and questions arising therefrom have been answered, competitors should be permitted to conduct an orderly inspection ("walkthrough") of the course of fire. The duration of time for the inspection must be stipulated by the Range Officer, and it should be the same for all competitors. If the course of fire includes moving targets or similar items, these should be demonstrated to all competitors for the same duration and frequency.

chunks.label: Rule 3.3.1
chunks.text: IPSC matches are governed by the rules applicable to the discipline. Host organizations may not enforce local rules except to comply with legislation or legal precedent in the applicable jurisdiction. Any voluntarily adopted rules that are not in compliance with these rules must not be applied to IPSC matches without the express consent of the Regional Director and the IPSC Executive Council.

chunks.label: Rule 4.1.1
chunks.text: Only targets approved by the IPSC Assembly and which fully comply with the specifications in Appendices B and C, and frangible targets (see Rule 4.5.1), are to be used for IPSC Shotgun matches.

chunks.label: Rule 4.1.1.1
chunks.text: If one or more targets at a match fail to comply exactly with the stated specifications, and if replacement targets of the correct specifications are unavailable, the Range Master must decide whether or not the variance is acceptable for that match, and which provisions of Section 2.3 of these rules will apply, if any. However, the Range Master's decision will only affect the match in progress, and will not serve as a precedent for future matches held at the same location, or for any subsequent use of the subject targets at another match.

chunks.label: Rule 4.1.1.2
chunks.text:
There are two sizes of paper targets and poppers approved for use in IPSC matches (see Appendices B and C). IPSC Mini Targets and Mini Poppers are used to simulate IPSC Targets and Poppers placed at greater distances. The following types and sizes of targets may be included together in the same target array:
 IPSC Targets and IPSC Poppers; or  IPSC Mini Targets and IPSC Mini Poppers; or  IPSC Targets and IPSC Mini Poppers; or  IPSC Mini Targets and IPSC Poppers.
The following types and sizes of targets must not be included together in the same target array:
 IPSC Targets and IPSC Mini Targets; or  IPSC Poppers and IPSC Mini Poppers.

chunks.label: Rule 4.1.2
chunks.text: Scoring targets used in all IPSC matches must be of a single color, as follows:

chunks.label: Rule 4.1.2.1
chunks.text: The scoring area of the IPSC Target and Mini Target must be tan colored, except where the Range Master deems that a lack of contrast with the surrounding area or background necessitates that a different color be used.

chunks.label: Rule 4.1.2.2
chunks.text: The entire front of scoring metal targets may either be painted a single color, preferably white, or may be unpainted.

chunks.label: Rule 4.1.3
chunks.text: No-shoots must be clearly marked with a conspicuous "X" or be of a single, unique color different from scoring targets throughout a match or tournament. Paper and metal no-shoots may be of different colors in a match or tournament provided that the chosen color is consistent for all no-shoots of the same material (i.e. if metal no-shoots are yellow, they must all be yellow and if paper no-shoots are white, they must all be white in a match or tournament).

chunks.label: Rule 4.1.4
chunks.text: Targets used in a course of fire may be partially or wholly hidden through the use of hard cover, as follows:

chunks.label: Rule 4.1.4.1
chunks.text: Cover provided to hide all or a portion of a target will be considered hard cover. When possible hard cover should not be simulated but constructed using impenetrable materials (see Rule 2.1.3). Hard cover must not be in the shape of a whole IPSC target.

chunks.label: Rule 4.1.5
chunks.text: Declaring a single, intact target to represent two or more targets by use of tape, paint or any other means and/or attaching a Mini Target to a full size target is prohibited.

chunks.label: Rule 4.1.6
chunks.text: Only IPSC targets, and mechanically or electrically operated devices, can be used to activate moving targets.

chunks.label: Rule 4.2.1
chunks.text: There are five paper targets approved for use in IPSC Shotgun matches (see Appendix B).

chunks.label: Rule 4.2.1.1
chunks.text: The Universal, the A4/A and the A3/B targets may be included together with other paper targets in the same course of fire.

chunks.label: Rule 4.2.2
chunks.text: Paper targets must have scoring lines and 0.5 cm (Mini Targets 0.3 cm) non-scoring borders clearly marked on the front of the target. However, scoring lines and non-scoring borders should not be visible beyond a distance of 10 meters.

chunks.label: Rule 4.2.2.1
chunks.text: The front of paper no-shoots must include a sufficiently distinguishable non-scoring border. In the absence of perforations or other suitable markings, the Range Master must ensure that all affected no-shoots have a replacement 0.5 cm (Mini Targets 0.3 cm) non-scoring border drawn or fitted thereon.

chunks.label: Rule 4.2.3
chunks.text: When the scoring area of a paper target is to be partially hidden, Course Designers must simulate hard cover in one of the following ways:

chunks.label: Rule 4.2.3.1
chunks.text: By actually hiding a portion of the target (see Rule 4.1.4.1); or

chunks.label: Rule 4.2.3.2
chunks.text: By physically cutting targets from edge to edge to remove the portion deemed to be hidden by hard cover. Such targets must be fitted with a replacement 0.5 cm (Mini Targets 0.3 cm) non-scoring border, which must extend the full width of the edge of the cut scoring area (see Rule 4.2.2); or

chunks.label: Rule 4.2.3.3
chunks.text: By painting or taping, with a sharply defined boundary, the portion of the target deemed to be hidden by hard cover with a single and visibly contrasting color.

chunks.label: Rule 4.2.3.4
chunks.text: When paper targets are partially hidden, physically cut, painted and/or taped, at least a portion of all scoring zones must remain visible.

chunks.label: Rule 4.2.4
chunks.text: Hard cover (and overlapping no-shoots) must not completely hide the A zone on a partially hidden paper target.

chunks.label: Rule 4.3.1
chunks.title: General Rules
chunks.text: General Rules

chunks.label: Rule 4.3.1.1
chunks.text: Metal targets and no-shoots which can accidentally turn edge-on or sideways when hit are expressly prohibited. Using them may result in withdrawal of IPSC sanction.

chunks.label: Rule 4.3.1.2
chunks.text: Metal targets and no-shoots which a Range Officer deems have fallen or overturned due to being hit on the apparatus supporting them, or for any other accidental reason (e.g. wind action, a ricochet, being hit solely by a shotgun wad etc.), will be treated as range equipment failure (see Rule 4.7.1).

chunks.label: Rule 4.3.1.3
chunks.text: Metal targets and no-shoots do not have a non-scoring border.

chunks.label: Rule 4.3.1.4
chunks.text: Metal targets and no-shoots must be shot and fall, overturn or self-indicate to score.

chunks.label: Rule 4.3.2
chunks.title: IPSC Poppers
chunks.text: IPSC Poppers

chunks.label: Rule 4.3.2.1
chunks.text: IPSC Poppers and IPSC Mini Poppers are both approved metal targets designed to recognize power, and must be calibrated as specified in Appendix C1.

chunks.label: Rule 4.3.3
chunks.title: IPSC Plates
chunks.text: IPSC Plates

chunks.label: Rule 4.3.3.1
chunks.text: Metal plates of various sizes may be used (see Appendix C3).

chunks.label: Rule 4.3.3.2
chunks.text: Not applicable.

chunks.label: Rule 4.3.3.3
chunks.text: Metal plates which fail to fall or overturn when initially hit, but which fall or overturn when hit with a subsequent shot, are not subject to a reshoot.

chunks.label: Rule 4.3.4
chunks.title: No-Shoots
chunks.text: No-Shoots

chunks.label: Rule 4.3.4.1
chunks.text: Metal no-shoot poppers and plates, must be shot and fall, overturn or self-indicate to score. If hit, they should be repainted during the scoring process.

chunks.label: Rule 4.5.1
chunks.text: Frangible targets, such as clay pigeons or tiles, may be used as scoring targets, but not as no-shoots, in IPSC Shotgun matches.

chunks.label: Rule 4.5.2
chunks.text: Synthetic targets (e.g. "self-sealing" targets etc.), sometimes used by indoor ranges, must not be used at Level III or higher matches. However, subject to the prior written approval of a Regional Director, synthetic targets may be used at Level I and II matches held within his Region.

chunks.label: Rule 4.6.1
chunks.section: 4.6 Rearrangement of Range Equipment or Surface
chunks.text: The competitor must not interfere with the range surface, natural foliage, constructions, props or other range equipment (including targets, target stands and target activators) at any time. Violations may incur one procedural penalty per occurrence at the discretion of the Range Officer.

chunks.label: Rule 4.6.2
chunks.section: 4.6 Rearrangement of Range Equipment or Surface
chunks.text: A competitor may request that Match Officials take corrective actions to ensure consistency in respect of the range surface, the presentation of targets and/or any other matter. The Range Master will have final authority concerning all such requests.

chunks.label: Rule 4.7.1
chunks.section: 4.7 Range Equipment Failure and Other Issues
chunks.text: Range equipment must present the challenge fairly and equitably to all competitors. Range equipment failure includes, but is not limited to, the displacement of paper targets, the premature activation of metal or moving targets, the malfunction of mechanically or electrically operated equipment, and the failure of props such as openings, ports, and barriers.

chunks.label: Rule 4.7.1.1
chunks.section: 4.7 Range Equipment Failure and Other Issues
chunks.text: The declaration and/or use of any firearm as range equipment is prohibited.

chunks.label: Rule 4.7.2
chunks.section: 4.7 Range Equipment Failure and Other Issues
chunks.text: A competitor who is unable to complete a course of fire due to range equipment failure, or if a metal or moving target was not reset prior to his attempt at a course of fire, must be required to reshoot the course of fire after corrective actions have been taken.

chunks.label: Rule 4.7.2.1
chunks.section: 4.7 Range Equipment Failure and Other Issues
chunks.text: Unrestored paper targets are not range equipment failure (see Rule 9.1.4).

chunks.label: Rule 4.7.2.2
chunks.section: 4.7 Range Equipment Failure and Other Issues
chunks.text: If a Range Master deems that one or more targets in a course of fire are faulty and/or have been presented in a manner significantly different to earlier presentations, he may offer a reshoot to the affected competitor(s).

chunks.label: Rule 4.7.3
chunks.section: 4.7 Range Equipment Failure and Other Issues
chunks.text: Chronic malfunction of equipment in a course of fire may result in the removal of that stage from the match results (see Rule 2.3.4).

chunks.label: Rule 5.1.1
chunks.text: Firearms are regulated by Divisions (see Appendix D), but courses of fire must remain consistent for all Divisions.

chunks.label: Rule 5.1.2
chunks.text: The minimum caliber for shotguns used in IPSC matches is 20 gauge (20 bore).

chunks.label: Rule 5.1.3
chunks.title:
Sights
Types of sights identified by IPSC are
chunks.text:
Sights
Types of sights identified by IPSC are:

chunks.label: Rule 5.1.3.1
chunks.text: "Open sights" are aiming devices fitted to a firearm which do not use electronic circuitry and/or lenses. Fiber-optic inserts are deemed not to be lenses.

chunks.label: Rule 5.1.3.2
chunks.text: "Optical/electronic sights" are aiming devices (including flashlights) fitted to a firearm which use electronic circuitry and/or lenses.

chunks.label: Rule 5.1.3.3
chunks.text: "Laser sights" are aiming devices fitted to a firearm that project a beam onto the target, providing a visual reference point. They are not permitted in IPSC matches.

chunks.label: Rule 5.1.3.4
chunks.text: The Range Master is the final authority in respect of the classification of any sights used in an IPSC match and/or their compliance with these rules, including the Divisions in Appendix D.

chunks.label: Rule 5.1.4
chunks.text: Unless required by a Division (see Appendix D), there is no restriction on the trigger pull weight of a firearm, but the trigger mechanism must, at all times, function safely.

chunks.label: Rule 5.1.5
chunks.text: Triggers and/or trigger shoes that extend beyond the width of the trigger guard are expressly prohibited. However, shotguns fitted with "winter triggers/guards" may be used in this mode, provided that this fitting was designed, manufactured and provided as part of the shotgun and only when the particular climate or weather conditions dictate their use.

chunks.label: Rule 5.1.6
chunks.text: Firearms must be serviceable and safe. Range Officers may demand examination of a competitor's firearm or allied equipment, at any time, to check they are functioning safely. If any such item is declared unserviceable or unsafe by a Range Officer, it must be withdrawn from the match until the item is repaired to the satisfaction of the Range Master (also see Rule 5.7.5).

chunks.label: Rule 5.1.7
chunks.text: Competitors must use the same firearm, barrel and type of sights for all courses of fire in a match. This includes magazine tubes which must not be changed unless they are changed as part of routine reloading during a course of fire. However, in the event that a competitor's original firearm and/or sights become unserviceable or unsafe during a match, the competitor must, before using a substitute firearm and/or sights, seek permission from the Range Master who may approve the substitution provided he is satisfied:

chunks.label: Rule 5.1.7.1
chunks.text: The substitute firearm satisfies the requirements of the relevant Division and is of the same type, action and caliber and is fitted with the same type of sights; and

chunks.label: Rule 5.1.7.2
chunks.text: In using the substitute firearm the competitor will not gain an advantage; and

chunks.label: Rule 5.1.7.3
chunks.text: The competitor's ammunition, when tested in the substitute firearm, attains the minimum power factor.

chunks.label: Rule 5.1.8
chunks.text: A competitor who substitutes or significantly modifies a firearm and/or sights during a match without the prior approval of the Range Master will be subject to the provisions of Rule 10.6.1.

chunks.label: Rule 5.1.9
chunks.text: A competitor must never use or wear on his person more than one firearm during a course of fire (see Rule 10.5.8).

chunks.label: Rule 5.1.10
chunks.text: The shotgun must be fitted with a stock enabling it to be fired from the shoulder (see Rule 10.5.16).

chunks.label: Rule 5.1.11
chunks.text: Firearms offering "burst" and/or fully automatic operation (i.e. whereby more than one round can be discharged on a single pull or activation of the trigger) are prohibited. Firearms fitted with a trigger where one round is discharged upon pulling the trigger and another round discharged upon releasing the trigger are also prohibited (see Rule 10.5.16).

chunks.label: Rule 5.1.12
chunks.text: Combination guns offering an additional barrel, or barrels, that is not a conventional shotgun barrel (e.g. a shotgun and rifle combination) are prohibited.

chunks.label: Rule 5.2.1
chunks.section: 5.2 Carry and Storage and Competitor Equipment
chunks.title: Carry and Storage
chunks.text: Carry and Storage – Except when within the boundaries of a Safety Area, or when under the supervision and direct command of a Range Officer, long guns must be unloaded and held, shouldered or slung (or placed in a rack), with the muzzle pointed skywards. Long guns placed in a slip or case are not required to be pointed skywards. Failure to comply may be subject to the provisions of Rule 10.5.1. The action may be open or closed, but a chamber safety flag must be fitted at all times when the firearm is not in use. Detachable magazines must be removed. Violations will incur a warning for the first occurrence, but will be subject to Rule 10.5.1 for subsequent occurrences in the same match.

chunks.label: Rule 5.2.1.1
chunks.section: 5.2 Carry and Storage and Competitor Equipment
chunks.text: Competitors arriving at an IPSC match in possession of a loaded firearm must immediately report to a Range Officer, who will supervise unloading of the firearm. Competitors failing to comply may be subject to Rule 10.5.14.

chunks.label: Rule 5.2.1.2
chunks.section: 5.2 Carry and Storage and Competitor Equipment
chunks.text: Within the provisions of Rule 5.2.1 no ammunition of any kind is permitted on the gun, or in clips or loops fitted to the gun, or to a sling fitted to the gun except when under the supervision of, and in response to a direct instruction issued by a Range Officer.

chunks.label: Rule 5.2.2
chunks.section: 5.2 Carry and Storage and Competitor Equipment
chunks.text: Not applicable.

chunks.label: Rule 5.2.3
chunks.section: 5.2 Carry and Storage and Competitor Equipment
chunks.text: Unless otherwise specified in the written stage briefing the competitor's equipment belt carrying cartridges (in caddies, loops, clips, bags or pouches) and/or detachable magazines and/or speed loaders must be worn at waist level. "Chest-rigs", bandoliers and similar carriers are expressly prohibited. Additional ammunition carriers mounted on forearms are permitted provided that cartridges are carried individually in loops or clips.

chunks.label: Rule 5.2.3.1
chunks.section: 5.2 Carry and Storage and Competitor Equipment
chunks.text: Not applicable.

chunks.label: Rule 5.2.3.2
chunks.section: 5.2 Carry and Storage and Competitor Equipment
chunks.text: Only one equipment carrying belt is permitted. Cartridges held in loops or clips on the belt are restricted to a maximum of 170 mm total height. Rounds carried in caddies (often known as "strippers") must not exceed 6 rounds in height.

chunks.label: Rule 5.2.3.3
chunks.section: 5.2 Carry and Storage and Competitor Equipment
chunks.text: The Range Master may make allowances for variations to Rule 5.2.3 due to anatomical considerations. The Range Master's decision on conformity to Rule 5.2.3 is final.

chunks.label: Rule 5.2.4
chunks.section: 5.2 Carry and Storage and Competitor Equipment
chunks.text: Ammunition and speed loaders must be carried on the competitor or gun in pouches, pockets, loops, clips or other suitable retention devices, unless otherwise specified in the written stage briefing. Loops, clips or other suitable retention devices fitted to the gun, or to a sling fitted to the gun, to hold individual cartridges or speed loaders are specifically permitted.

chunks.label: Rule 5.2.5
chunks.section: 5.2 Carry and Storage and Competitor Equipment
chunks.text: When carried in loops, clips or caddies no part of any cartridge is permitted to extend further than 75 mm from a competitor's belt. Cartridges carried on the gun are exempt and loose cartridges carried in a pouch or bag are usually exempt from this rule. The Range Master's decision will be final in this matter. Open Division competitors are exempt from this rule.

chunks.label: Rule 5.2.5.1
chunks.section: 5.2 Carry and Storage and Competitor Equipment
chunks.text: The measurement is to be taken while the competitor is standing naturally upright.

chunks.label: Rule 5.2.5.2
chunks.section: 5.2 Carry and Storage and Competitor Equipment
chunks.text: Any competitor who fails the foregoing test prior to the Start Signal will be required to immediately adjust his belt, equipment or cartridges to achieve compliance. The Range Master may make allowances for variations in these requirements due to anatomical considerations. Some competitors may not be able to fully comply.

chunks.label: Rule 5.2.6
chunks.section: 5.2 Carry and Storage and Competitor Equipment
chunks.text: Not applicable.

chunks.label: Rule 5.2.7
chunks.section: 5.2 Carry and Storage and Competitor Equipment
chunks.text: Not applicable.

chunks.label: Rule 5.2.8
chunks.section: 5.2 Carry and Storage and Competitor Equipment
chunks.text: Equipment (including slings regardless of whether they can also carry cartridges) that is only used when fitted to the shotgun (except chokes, ammunition, speed loaders and ammunition carriers) and is to be used at any time during any COF must be fitted to the shotgun for every COF in the match.

chunks.label: Rule 5.3.1
chunks.text: The use of camouflage or other similar types of military or police garments other than by competitors who are law enforcement or military personnel is discouraged. The Match Director will be the final authority in respect of what garments must not be worn by competitors.

chunks.label: Rule 5.4.1
chunks.text: All persons are warned that the correct use of adequate eye and ear protection is in their own interest and of paramount importance to prevent injury to vision and hearing. It is strongly recommended that eye and ear protection be worn at all times by all persons while on the range premises.

chunks.label: Rule 5.4.2
chunks.text: Host organizations may require the use of such protection by all persons, as a condition of attendance and while present on the range premises. If so, Match Officials must make every reasonable effort to ensure that all persons wear adequate protection.

chunks.label: Rule 5.4.3
chunks.text: If a Range Officer notices that a competitor has lost or displaced their eye or ear protection during a course of fire, or has commenced a course of fire without them, the Range Officer must immediately stop the competitor who will be required to reshoot the course of fire after the protective devices have been restored.

chunks.label: Rule 5.4.4
chunks.text: A competitor who inadvertently loses eye or ear protection during a course of fire, or commences a course of fire without them, is entitled to stop, point their firearm in a safe direction and indicate the problem to the Range Officer, in which case the provisions of the previous rule will apply.

chunks.label: Rule 5.4.5
chunks.text: Any attempt to gain a reshoot or advantage by removing eye and/or ear protection during a course of fire will be considered unsportsmanlike conduct (see Rule 10.6.2).

chunks.label: Rule 5.4.6
chunks.text: If a Range Officer deems that a competitor about to make an attempt at a course of fire is wearing inadequate eye or ear protection, the Range Officer may order the competitor to rectify the situation before allowing the competitor to continue. The Range Master is the final authority on this matter.

chunks.label: Rule 5.5.1
chunks.text: Competitors at an IPSC match are solely and personally responsible for the safety of all and any ammunition, which they bring to the match.
